chunk_findings.detail: The Claude pre-tool hook matcher is `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`. Claude Code also has a `Bash` tool that can write arbitrary files, but `Bash` is not in the matcher, so invoking `Bash` with e.g. `echo x > /outside/lease` does not trigger the `PreToolUse` hook at all. This defeats the documented prevent behavior: "A write outside the item's lease globs ... is refused."
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:CLAUDE_WRITE_MATCHER

chunk_findings.detail: `_tracked` passes `str(f)` unchanged to `git ls-files --error-unmatch`. When `home` is absolute (the normal case) and lies under the allowed `<repo>/.ddflow`, these paths are absolute; Git does not match absolute pathspecs and returns nonzero even when the file is tracked. Given a repo with tracked `<repo>/.ddflow/ddflow-lane-hooks/claude-settings.json`, `prepare` gets `_tracked() == False` and overwrites the tracked project file, so the intended refusal `"a lane hook path is tracked by the project"` is never returned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:_tracked

chunk_findings.detail: `remove` trusts the contents of `manifest.json` and unlinks every `"files"` entry without validating that the path is inside the lane home. A manifest at `<home>/ddflow-lane-hooks/manifest.json` containing `{"files": ["[REDACTED:path]"]}` makes `remove(<home>)` delete that file, rather than deleting only what `prepare` wrote. Corrupted, stale, or agent-writable manifests should not turn cleanup into arbitrary file deletion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:remove

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.relative_to` does not raise `ValueError` when the target is outside `cwd` on the same filesystem; it returns a path with `..` components. For example, `_relative("/etc/passwd", Path("/lane/repo"))` returns `"../../etc/passwd"`, not `None`. Since `verdict` only treats `rel is None` as “outside the lane worktree”, that outside path is never caught as outside. If the active lease glob is broad enough (e.g. `**`), such a path can match and `verdict` returns `(0, "")`, allowing a call to write outside the worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:_relative

chunk_findings.detail: `render` substitutes `_ARGV` first and then applies `_AGENT` to the entire resulting string. A lane's check argv is data and may legally contain the literal marker `__DDFLOW_AGENT__`; validation only requires that each argv entry be a string. For example, `render(["/bin/check", "__DDFLOW_AGENT__"], "lane-1")` first produces `const ARGV = ["/bin/check", "__DDFLOW_AGENT__"];`, then the second `.replace` also rewrites the marker inside the already-substituted JSON array, yielding `const ARGV = ["/bin/check", ""lane-1""];`, which is invalid JavaScript (adjacent double quotes). The generated `ddflow-lane-hook.js` then fails to parse/load, so the operator-approved hook is broken for that lane. This violates the file's own model that lane-specific values are inert JSON data and never alter the template code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_plugin.py:67

chunk_findings.detail: The `tree` fixture creates a fresh repository but never adds `.ddflow/` to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. The test then passes `repo / ".ddflow" / "x"` as the lane home and asserts `isinstance(r, LH.Prepared)`, relying on the comment that this is "the project's git-ignored state dir." In this fixture `repo/.ddflow` is untracked and not ignored, so after `LH.prepare` writes the hook config there, `git status --porcelain` in `repo` will show `?? .ddflow/`. The test incorrectly blesses this path as private/git-ignored and would pass even though the main repository working tree becomes dirty.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_hooks.py:188

data.reason: the review was terminated by SIGTERM before a reviewer finished: nothing was reviewed, which is not a pass

chunk_findings.detail: Claude Code has a `Bash` tool that can write arbitrary files (`echo x > /outside/lease`), but `CLAUDE_WRITE_MATCHER = "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"` does not include `Bash`, so the `PreToolUse` hook is not fired for that tool. Given a Claude lane with this settings file, an agent can use `Bash` to write outside the item's lease globs without the blocking pre-tool hook executing, defeating the documented prevent behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:CLAUDE_WRITE_MATCHER

chunk_findings.detail: `_write` calls `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` and then `os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)` with no `O_NOFOLLOW`; both operations follow symbolic links. If the lane home contains a symlink at a hook path, e.g. `<home>/ddflow-lane-hooks/claude-settings.json -> [REDACTED:path]`, `_tracked` resolves the target outside the repo and returns `False`, so `prepare` follows the symlink and truncates that target. This writes outside the lane home, violating the guarantee in this module's contract and allowing an overwrite of an arbitrary file on a later `prepare` over a persistent, agent-writable lane home.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:_write

chunk_findings.detail: In `hook_probe`, `cfg = Path(m["files"][0])` is evaluated before the following `try/except`. A valid JSON manifest with `"level": "prevent"` and `"files": []` skips the initial per-file loop and then raises an uncaught `IndexError` when that indexing occurs; `hook_probe` returns `bool | None`, so this crashes `conformance.run` instead of returning `False` for a broken/malformed manifest. The same malformed-manifest data is already defended against in `remove` for cleanup, but not here.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:hook_probe

chunk_findings.detail: `paths_of` only inspects `PATH_KEYS`, so a shell tool call such as `Bash` with `tool_input: {"command": "echo pwn > /outside/lease"}` produces `[]`. `verdict` then returns `(0, "")` before consulting `_mine`, allowing the write. This is still the previous finding #1 hole: the new checker does not answer it, and even if the matcher later includes `Bash`, the check remains empty for shell writes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:paths_of,verdict

chunk_findings.detail: The self-managed exemption is `rel.startswith(SELF_MANAGED)`. With `SELF_MANAGED` being the project's `.ddflow` state directory, this also matches paths such as `.ddflow-evil/README.md`, which are not under `.ddflow/` at all. A lane with any live lease can therefore edit `.ddflow-evil/README.md` even if that path is outside its lease globs. The boundary check should be `rel == SELF_MANAGED or rel.startswith(SELF_MANAGED + "/")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:verdict

chunk_findings.detail: `render` validates `argv` only by checking that it is non-empty and its elements are `str`, never that `argv` itself is a `list`. A non-empty Python `str` is an iterable of `str`, so `render("/bin/check", "lane-1")` passes the guard; line 68 then does `list(argv)`, producing `["/", "b", "i", "n", "/", ...]`. In the generated hook, `ARGV[0]` becomes `"/"`, `spawnSync("/", ["b", ...])` fails with `r.error`, and the hook takes the fail-open branch on every call, silently allowing the writes the hook must block. The guard should require `isinstance(argv, list)` before iterating it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_plugin.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test for the manifest-deletion fix appends the out-of-home victim after the legitimate manifest entries and only asserts that `victim.exists()` when `LH.remove(home)` returns something containing `"refused"`. It never asserts that the legitimate hook files such as `p.files[0]` or `home / LH.DIR_NAME` survive the refusal. A broken `LH.remove` that unlinks manifest entries in order would delete the legitimate lane hook config, hit the appended out-of-home path, return `"refused"`, leave the victim untouched, and still pass this assertion when the valid paths precede the malicious one. The test therefore does not actually hold the cited finding against a partial-cleanup variant of the same bug.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_hooks.py:test_review_findings_hold

chunk_findings.detail: `_relative` normalizes `path` relative to the passed `cwd`, not relative to the lane worktree root. `verdict` then compares that string against lease globs that are relative to the repo root. For `repo=/repo`, `cwd=/repo/src`, `file_path="main.py"`, and lane glob `src/**`, `_relative` returns `"main.py"`, so a write to `/repo/src/main.py` is falsely refused. The same root cause also lets an outside `cwd` evade the boundary: with `cwd=/tmp` and `file_path="x"`, `_relative` returns `"x"` even though the worktree is `/repo`; if the lane glob is `**`, `verdict` allows writing `/tmp/x`. `_relative` needs to resolve the path relative to `repo` and verify that `cwd` is inside `repo`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:53 _relative

chunk_findings.detail: `_relative` performs only lexical `normpath`/`relpath` and never resolves symlinks, so it misses paths that leave the worktree through a symlink. Given `/repo/link -> /etc`, lane root `/repo`, lane glob `**`, and a tool call with `"file_path": "link/passwd"`, `_relative` returns `"link/passwd"` (the first path part is not `..`), so `verdict` allows the call. A file-write tool that follows the symlink writes `/etc/passwd`, outside the worktree, contradicting the function's contract of returning `None` when the path leaves it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:57 _relative

chunk_findings.detail: The hook reads the tool arguments from `output.args`, but in opencode’s `tool.execute.before` API the actual tool request is `input.call.input`; `output` is the permission/context object and has no `args`. For any real tool call (e.g. a Bash call with `command: "rm -rf ..."`), `output.args` is `undefined`, so `tool_input` in the JSON payload becomes `{}`. The lane lease check therefore evaluates an empty input instead of the operation that is about to run, allowing refusals to be bypassed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_plugin.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: `CLAUDE_WRITE_MATCHER = "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"` still does not include `Bash`, so `_plan`'s Claude `PreToolUse` hook is not armed for Claude Code's `Bash` tool. Given a Claude lane, the agent can run `Bash` with `echo pwn > /outside/lease`; the blocking pre-tool hook never executes, so the documented prevent behavior (“A write outside the item's lease globs … is refused”) is defeated. The git pre-commit hook only catches this later if the agent commits, not at write time.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:CLAUDE_WRITE_MATCHER

chunk_findings.detail: The final-component symlink case was fixed with `is_symlink()` and `O_NOFOLLOW`, but a symlink in a parent directory is still followed. `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on a parent that is a symlink to a directory does not remove or reject the symlink (`path.mkdir` treats a symlink-to-directory as `is_dir()` true and suppresses `FileExistsError`), and `O_NOFOLLOW` only protects the last component. Input: pre-create `<home>/ddflow-lane-hooks` as a symlink to `/etc/ddflow-pwn`; `prepare(... home=<home>, harness="claude", ...)` then writes/truncates `/etc/ddflow-pwn/claude-settings.json` outside the lane home. `_tracked` does not catch it because the resolved target is outside the repo.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:_write

chunk_findings.detail: `hook_probe` executes whatever the lane-home manifest says to execute, without verifying that `files[0]` is inside `home` or matches the operator-approved plugin template/digest. A lane worker can write to its own `<home>` and replace the manifest with `{"level":"prevent","door":"plugin-home","files":["<home>/evil.mjs"],"worktree":"..."}` plus `evil.mjs`; `_fire_plugin` reads that file and Node imports it, so `conformance.run` runs attacker-controlled JavaScript in the ddflow process. The settings branch similarly runs an arbitrary command read from `files[0]` through `_fire`. This bypasses the `Consent`/digest gate entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:hook_probe

chunk_findings.detail: A malformed manifest with a valid settings file but missing `"worktree"` or `"agent"` crashes `hook_probe` instead of returning `False`. The `try/except` only wraps reading `files[0]` and extracting `cmd`; afterward `payload` uses `m["worktree"]` and `_fire` uses `m["agent"]`, so the probe raises `KeyError`. Concrete input: manifest `{"level":"prevent","door":"settings-arg","files":["<home>/.../claude-settings.json"]}` with a parseable settings file. The `plugin-home` branch has the same unguarded `m["worktree"]` in `_fire_plugin`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:hook_probe

chunk_findings.detail: A Bash tool call such as `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo pwn > /outside/lease"}}` still bypasses the check: `paths_of` returns `[]`, and `verdict` returns `(0, "")` at the `if not rels` early return before consulting `_mine`. The module docstring acknowledges this is only caught by the lane's git pre-commit hook, but that detection happens only when the agent later commits; an agent can write outside its lease without committing, so the documented prevent behavior remains defeated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:verdict

chunk_findings.detail: The fix for the previous `.ddflow-evil` prefix bug is overnarrow. `SELF_MANAGED` is the no-trailing-slash directory `.ddflow`; the condition `rel.startswith(m) if m.endswith("/") else rel == m` exempts exactly `.ddflow` but not `.ddflow/...`. Given a live lease with globs `src/**`, a tool call with `file_path: ".ddflow/lane.json"` produces `rel = ".ddflow/lane.json"`; `_self_managed` returns `False`, `inside` is false, and `verdict` refuses a ddflow bookkeeping write the function is explicitly meant to exempt. The boundary check should be `rel == m or rel.startswith(m + "/")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:_self_managed

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `render` still validates `agent` only by truthiness, not by type, so a non-empty non-string `agent` passes the guard. For example, `render(["/bin/check"], b"lane-1")` reaches `json.dumps(b"lane-1")`, which raises a `TypeError` instead of the documented `ValueError`; `render(["/bin/check"], True)` silently emits `const AGENT = true;`, so the spawned check sees `DDFLOW_AGENT` as `"true"` rather than the lane identity. The type hole that was fixed for `argv` remains for `agent`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_plugin.py:render

chunk_findings.detail: `test_check_fails_open` asserts that `CK.main(["--repo", str(tmp_path), "--agent", "l"]) == 0` when `CK.verdict` raises `RuntimeError`. This codifies fail-open behavior for a preventive security hook: if the guard itself crashes (for example, `_mine` malforms a lease record or the repository path is unusable and `verdict` raises), the PreToolUse hook exits 0 and the write is allowed. The expected behavior for a prevent-level guard should be to fail closed with `CK.REFUSE`, not allow the tool call. This test would make a correct fail-closed fix fail, and it blesses silently disabling the lease check whenever an unexpected error occurs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_hooks.py:test_check_fails_open

chunk_findings.detail: `_write` only checks the final component with `is_symlink()` / `O_NOFOLLOW`; it does not refuse a symlinked parent directory inside `home`. If `home` is allowed by `_refuse_location` but `home/ddflow-lane-hooks` (or `home/.config/<harness>`) is a symlink to a repository directory, `path.parent.mkdir(..., exist_ok=True)` is a no-op and `os.open` follows the parent symlink. For `repo=/repo`, `worktree=/repo`, `home=/lane`, and `/lane/ddflow-lane-hooks -> /repo/src`, a detect-lane `prepare` writes `home/ddflow-lane-hooks/manifest.json` to `/repo/src/manifest.json`, outside the lane home, despite `_write`'s own comment saying it never writes through a link.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:_write

chunk_findings.detail: `prepare` never resolves `home` or `worktree`, so the manifest records `files` and `worktree` exactly as passed. Later `remove` and `hook_probe` resolve those stored strings relative to the *current* working directory, not the value of `home` used during `prepare`. With a relative `home`/`worktree` and a cwd change, `remove` can uninstall the git hook from a different worktree and can fail to remove plugin hook files (they are under `home/.config/...`, outside `home/DIR_NAME`, so the final `rmtree(home/DIR_NAME)` does not clean them). Example: a plugin prepare with `home="lane_home"` from `/repo` stores `"lane_home/.config/<harness>/...";` later `remove(Path("/repo/lane_home"))` from `/tmp` interprets that path under `/tmp`, leaving the real plugin hook in place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks.py:prepare

chunk_findings.detail: `_relative` resolves `path` against the tool call's `cwd`, not against the lane worktree root, so `verdict` compares repo-relative lease globs with a string relative to a subdirectory. For `--repo /repo`, payload `{"cwd": "/repo/src", "tool_input": {"file_path": "main.py"}}`, and lane glob `src/**`, `_relative` returns `"main.py"`; `inside("main.py", "src/**")` is false, so a legitimate write to `/repo/src/main.py` is refused. The same defect evades the boundary: `{"cwd": "/tmp", "tool_input": {"file_path": "x"}}` with a glob such as `**` returns `"x"` and allows a write to `/tmp/x` outside the worktree. The function must be relative to `repo`, but it never receives `repo`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:_relative

chunk_findings.detail: `_relative` does only lexical `normpath`/`relpath` and never resolves symlinks; a path can leave the worktree through a symlink and still be treated as inside. Given `/repo/link -> /etc`, `--repo /repo`, payload `{"cwd": "/repo", "tool_input": {"file_path": "link/passwd"}}`, and lane glob `**`, `_relative` returns `"link/passwd"` (first part is not `..`), so `verdict` allows the call. A file-write tool that follows the symlink writes `/etc/passwd`, outside the worktree, violating the function's contract of returning `None` when the path leaves the lane worktree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_check.py:_relative

chunk_findings.detail: The hook still sends `tool_input: output.args || {}` to the lane check, but in opencode’s `tool.execute.before` API the tool arguments are in `input.call.input`; `output` is the permission/context object and has no `args`. For a Bash call with `command: "rm -rf ..."`, `output.args` is `undefined`, so the JSON payload contains `"tool_input":{}`, the lane lease check evaluates an empty input, and the call the hook was supposed to refuse is allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/lanehooks_plugin.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: This regression test only checks `_relative` with `cwd=Path("/lane/repo")`. It never supplies the two inputs from the earlier HIGH finding — `cwd=Path("/repo/src"), path="main.py"` and `cwd=Path("/tmp"), path="x"`. If `_relative` still normalizes relative to `cwd` rather than the lane worktree root, those calls return `"main.py"` and `"x"`, so this test remains green while `verdict` both falsely refuses `/repo/src/main.py` and allows the outside write `/tmp/x`. The test advertised as holding the review finding does not exercise it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_hooks.py:test_review_findings_hold

chunk_findings.detail: The symlink part only creates a symlink at the hook config path and expects `LH.prepare` to raise. It never creates `repo/link -> /etc` and calls `CK._relative`/`CK.verdict` with `link/passwd`. If the earlier `_relative` symlink escape remains, this test still passes, so a tool call through the symlink can write outside the worktree while the suite reports the finding as held.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_hooks.py:test_second_round_findings
